title: Advanced Participle Clauses
completion_message: ¡Brillante! Las 'Participle Clauses' son la herramienta secreta de los escritores y oradores avanzados. Te permiten condensar información, eliminar conjunciones innecesarias (como because o after) y darle a tu discurso un flujo rítmico y ejecutivo impecable.

parts.visual:
1. Present Participle (-ing): 
- Reemplaza 'because' / 'as' / 'since' (Razón). 
Ej: Being aware of the risks, we decided to proceed. (Como éramos conscientes de los riesgos...). 
- Acciones simultáneas. 
Ej: He sat at his desk, analyzing the data. (Se sentó... analizando...). 

2. Past Participle (-ed / 3ra columna): 
- Sentido pasivo o reemplaza 'if'. 
Ej: Seen from this angle, the project looks profitable. (Si se ve desde este ángulo...). 
Ej: Founded in 1990, the company has grown rapidly.
parts.audio: Welcome to Advanced Participle Clauses. These clauses allow us to condense information and sound highly professional. Number 1: Present Participle, the '-ing' form. We use it to replace 'because', 'as', or 'since' to show reason. For example: Being aware of the risks, we decided to proceed. It also shows simultaneous actions. For example: He sat at his desk, analyzing the data. Number 2: Past Participle, the '-ed' form or the third column. This has a passive meaning or replaces 'if'. For example: Seen from this angle, the project looks profitable. Or: Founded in 1990, the company has grown rapidly.

parts.visual:
3. Perfect Participle (Having + Past Participle): 
- Indica que una acción terminó ANTES de que empezara la siguiente. 
- Reemplaza 'After'. 
Ej: Having analyzed the market, we launched the product. (Después de haber analizado...). 
Ej: Not having received a reply, I sent a follow-up email. (Como no había recibido respuesta...). 

¡OJO! (Dangling Participles): 
El sujeto de la cláusula principal DEBE ser el mismo que el de la cláusula de participio. 
INCORRECTO: Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful. (¿Los árboles caminaban?). 
CORRECTO: Walking down the street, I saw the beautiful trees.
parts.audio: Number 3: Perfect Participle, which is 'Having' plus a Past Participle. This indicates that one action finished BEFORE the next one started. It replaces 'after'. For example: Having analyzed the market, we launched the product. Or in the negative: Not having received a reply, I sent a follow-up email. Be careful with Dangling Participles! The subject of the main clause MUST be the same as the subject of the participle clause. Incorrect: Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful. Trees don't walk! Correct: Walking down the street, I saw the beautiful trees.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la cláusula de participio correcta.

questions.question: ____ aware of the budget cuts, the manager cancelled the corporate retreat. (Como era consciente).
questions.explanation: Being aware of = As he was aware of.

questions.question: ____ from this perspective, the merger is actually a brilliant idea. (Si se ve).
questions.explanation: Seen from = If it is seen from (sentido pasivo).

questions.question: ____ reviewed all the resumes, HR decided to hire Sarah. (Después de haber revisado).
questions.explanation: Having reviewed = After they had reviewed (acción anterior terminada).

questions.question: ____ in 1920, the bank is one of the oldest in the country. (Fundado).
Not ____ received the funds, we cannot start construction. (Como no hemos recibido).
questions.explanation: Not having received = As we have not received (negación del perfect participle).

questions.question: ____ at her desk, she carefully analyzed the financial report. (Sentada - acción simultánea).
____ exhausted by the long negotiation, the CEO went straight to bed.
questions.explanation: Exhausted = As he was exhausted (pasado participio / adjetivo).

questions.question: ____ read the manual, he knew exactly how to fix the machine. (Como ya había leído).
questions.explanation: Having read = Because he had read (acción anterior).

questions.question: Which sentence has a Dangling Participle? (INCORRECTA por sujetos distintos).
options: Looking out the window, it started to rain.
Looking out the window, I saw the rain.
Having finished my dinner, I watched TV.
questions.correct_answer: Looking out the window, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: El sujeto de la principal es 'it' (el clima), pero 'it' no estaba mirando por la ventana. Es un error gramatical.

questions.question: ____ no other option, the company declared bankruptcy.
questions.explanation: Having no other option = As they had no other option.

questions.question: ____ in the heart of London, our office is easy to reach. (Situada).
Not ____ what to do, I asked my supervisor for advice. (No sabiendo).
questions.explanation: Not knowing = As I didn't know (razón presente).

questions.question: ____ out of the room, he slammed the door behind him. (Caminando - simultáneo).
____ the contract, I realized it contained a severe penalty clause. (Mientras leía).
____ been warned about the risks, they decided not to invest. (Después de haber sido advertidos - pasivo perfecto).
questions.explanation: Having been warned = After they had been warned.

questions.question: ____ by the sudden drop in sales, the board called an emergency meeting. (Preocupados/Alarmados).
questions.explanation: Alarmed = As they were alarmed (pasado participio).

questions.question: ____ a native speaker, she was able to translate the document perfectly. (Siendo).
questions.explanation: Being a native speaker = As she was a native speaker.

questions.question: ____ the password, he couldn't log into the server. (Habiendo olvidado).
questions.explanation: Having forgotten = Because he had forgotten (acción terminada previa).

questions.question: ____ carefully, the software should last for years without bugs. (Si es diseñado).
questions.explanation: Designed carefully = If it is designed carefully.

questions.question: ____ late for the meeting, I missed the CEO's opening remarks.
questions.explanation: Arriving late = As I arrived late.

questions.question: ____ aware of the risks, we stopped. (Como éramos conscientes - con B)
____ finished the report, I went home. (Después de haber terminado - con H)
____ from this angle, it's perfect. (Si se ve - con S)
Not ____ received an answer, I called. (Como no había recibido - con H)
____ no money, he couldn't buy it. (No teniendo - con H)
____ in 1990, the firm is huge. (Fundada - con F)
Not ____ what to do, I asked. (No sabiendo - con K)
____ at her desk, she worked. (Sentada - con S)
____ read the book, I knew the end. (Habiendo leído - con H)
____ been warned, he was careful. (Después de haber sido - con H)

pairs.target: Como era consciente de / Siendo consciente
Después de haber analizado los datos
Si se ve desde este ángulo
